COALITION POLITICS

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
This week the Democratic Alliance lost Nelson Mandela as their coalition partnerships are falling apart - is this the beginning of the end for the rest of the DA run municipalities?

Unique Selling Point:
CURRENT NEWS STORY

Further information:
We look at how the city of Nelson Mandela Bay got to this point - how the DA stole the city and lost it. We speak to Dr Crispian Olver - author who wrote about the rot within the city and then also speak to Athol Trollip the ousted Nelson Mandela Bay mayor, PE based political analyst Ongama Mtimka and the local EFF branch.

We take the issue wider looking at the JHB and PTA municipalities.

Victor Manyati

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: The ANC lost control of three of South Africa’s major metros in 2016.

Johannesburg, Tshwane and Nelson Mandela Bay were secured by the Democratic Alliance through coalition agreements with smaller parties.

RALPH: When you are engaged in coalitions, you are walking on eggshells, particularly when you share nothing concrete with the people you are in a coalition with.

VO: And as the 2019 elections creep up, the cracks - are starting to show.
UPSOUND JULIUS… DA voted against us – and we said a-ha – you think we are playing we are going for the white man in PE, we are going to cut the throat…(march 2018)
LINK: Earlier this week the Mayor of Nelson Mandela Bay metro, Athol Trollip got the boot – and a new Mayor – Mongameli BOBANI was elected, effectively putting the city into the hands of an EFF / ANC / UDM Alliance

OLVER: Strangely the revolt came from within the DA.

VO: The man of the moment is DA councillor Victor Manyati.

MANYATI: // I love DA – but I don’t love the behaviour of Trollip // that guy is not good to be a leader – he is not.// he treated me like a farm boy and I am not.

VO: Manyati tipped the balance when he abstained from voting in a motion to remove the speaker.

It appears that the DA is cannibalising itself.

LINK: it //set in motion a chain of events which saw the DA councillors leave the chamber, opening the door to a complete power shift.

VO: A new speaker was elected under the authority of the MEC. And then, without a single member of the DA in the room, the motion to remove Trollip was tabled….

UPSOUND: Vote vote….

VO: Trollip was out. And in a twist, the man he fired - his former UDM deputy mayor, Mongameli Bobani - was elected mayor.

DEREK Did you see the gap?
BOBANI: oh yes, yes, definitely so, definitely we saw the gap – right now they are short of numbers because their councillor abstained and then saw today is our day.

VO: Political analyst Ongama Mtimka believes the DA could have avoided this coup.

ONGAMA: Trollip // should have thought well about the fact that they didn’t have absolute power and managing political relationships was as important a task as driving a turn around in the administration.

VO: Trollip says the DA was blind sided.

TROLLIP: You can never plan for treachery in you own party // it is clear that councillor Manyati didn’t do this of his own volition // he was turned – I believe he was turned through financial inducement

MANYATI: If councillor Trollip knows where that money is I would appreciate it if he can bring that to me tomorrow – I will be in PE tomorrow and I will appreciate it if he can give me that money – I need it.

VO: Bribe or no bribe – Public Sector Expert Dr Crispian Olver believes it was a planned move that earned Mayor Bobani the top seat.

OLVER: He would know would very well that the ANC could never pull off a coalition without the UDM’s two seats in the council and he would have been demanding a very large price for those two seats and that price would have been a lot more than deputy mayor – it would have been mayor or bust.

VO: While the validity of these developments are being challenged by the DA - the city will remain in the hands of this newly formed alliance.

Mayor Bobani almost immediately appointed a brand new mayoral committee with mostly ANC councillors, one from the United Front and one from the EFF.

OLVER: //Looking at who the people are in that mayoral committee – it’s a largely untested mayoral committee – these are people that don’t have a lot of experience in government //

VO: It’s a joint effort driven by consultation explains Mayor Bobani.

BOBANI: There Is no winner here – // this is a collective government – so any decision that we are going to take – we are going to sit down and – there is no ANC here that is going to bulldoze // it is going to be a collective decision.

VO: But the DA is doubtful about the new team’s intentions.

TROLLIP: they’ve got a bad track record, they are very greedy and they cant wait to get their hands on the public purse that we’ve plumped up quite nicely.

VO: An allegation Mayor Bobani denies.

BOBANI: there will be no city coffers that will be raped – I mean for what – all that will happen is that they will get the service they have been hungry for //.

LINK: One of the charges levelled against the DA led municipality is that their policies were anti-poor and focussed on the affluent white suburbs rather than the informal settlements and the wider community.

TROLLIP: that is a complete falsehood – there is a prescript – 80% to poor – 20 % to the affluent – despite the fact that the rates comes from the affluent areas – you have to redress the past – the spatial reality of apartheid

VO: Mtimka agrees that the budgets have been spent, but believes the impact of municipal credit policies were not considered with the poor in mind.

ONGAMA: The government want to change it’s fiscal condition was too harsh on cutting services especially in townships where to recoup payment – that is one criticism I have heard not from politicians but from people.

VO: Manyati feels the issues run much deeper.

MANYATI: You cannot to have white man in south Africa to run a municipality or a province – it is wrong! Because the majority of the people are black – it’s wrong!

VO: But the EFF’s Eastern Cape convener, Marshall Dlamini says their main issue with the DA is around policy – specifically, land expropriation.

DLAMINI: // Once you start thinking that land must not go back to its original owner, its original people that owners of the land – then our relationship with you is finished.

VO: A position Trollip stands by.

TROLLIP: We believe South Africans should have the right to own property – we are not going to be swayed – even if that means me being removed.

LINK: Coalition politics is on shaky ground across the country – with smaller parties threatening the status quo in major metros and wielding their power as king makers.

ONGAMA: We are going to see more the use of the votes in local councils of very small parties who play king maker role – so if there is an issue at parliament//– is that in the best interest of people? Absolutely not – but that is the nature of politics, people augment their power elsewhere and try and use that to advance certain positions.

VO: And quite often it’s not about policies says political analyst Ralph Mathekga.

RALPH: You don’t see policy coalitions and as they stay in these coalitions and they are not getting policy influence they must be getting something else – that is where these arrangements are becoming quite questionable.

OLVER: The danger with these coalitions is that they become rent-seeking coalitions and they divide the municipality up into turf and they each feed on those respective turfs

VO: Besides Trollip, there have been multiple motions of no-confidence brought against the DA mayors in Johannesburg and Tshwane.

OLVER: The word is out that the EFF are flip flopping – they got into bed with the DA to get rid of the ANC, now they want to get rid of the DA and by default they are going to be bringing ANC led coalitions back into power.

VO: Dlamini refutes that they are putting the ANC back power.

DLAMINI: // it’s the voters that put the ANC back in power it’s not us. // We are not a flip flop party – we only deal with the principle // So when you start to misbehave that’s when we tell you straight that you are misbehaving and we cannot have that.

VO: But the motivations driving the EFF’s decisions have to be questioned argues Mtimka.

ONGAMA: What is given more weight – did the politics of clean governance, is it the politics of race, is it the politics of an arrogant DA that must be punished, or is it the politics of lets wield power whenever we can and whenever we can exploit particular narratives to advance ourselves.

LINK: On Thursday Solly Msimanga who was clinging to power in Tshwane and supporters of all parties took the streets before the crucial vote.

VO: The motion was denied and the vote did not take place – so Mayor Msimanga lives to fight another day.

DEREK Who stands to benefit from the coalitions crumbling?
OLVER: A lot of the contest is about access to resources – in cities where the leadership has held the line and kept people out of portfolios that happens to be the same cities now where the push is being made to get rid of the mayors and to get a new team in place

RALPH // if people think there is corruption at national level it’s just the tip of an iceberg – local gov way more complex and there is way more patronage being exchanged at local gov.

VO: The DA say this is a concern in Nelson Mandela Bay as they won the city after it was plagued by corruption under the previous ANC leadership.

TROLLIP: We are not going to hand this city back to people who want to steal it – we are going to challenge it in court//

VO: The new Nelson Mandela Bay alliance is not concerned about the legal challenge – they believe they followed procedure.

DLAMINI: The DA are just talking because they want to hold onto power with everything that they have// they are just cowards – we are not paying attention to them – they are not a threat to us, we are fighting to get political power in this country.

VO: But Olver warns, while political coalition agreements are unstable by nature, the changes don’t come without consequences.

OLVER: the one lesson that we’ve learnt from SANs voters is that they don’t like instability and the punish the parties that they see as driving that instability.



PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Nelson Mandela Bay Mayor Athol Trollip was given the boot in a dramatic collapse of coalition partnerships.

TROLLIP: You can never plan for treachery in you own party

PROMO 2
VO: Democratic Alliance mayors are in the firing line with unhappy political partners bringing motions of no-confidence against them. Is this the beginning of the end for coalition politics?

RALPH: When you are engaged in coalitions, you are walking on eggshells, particularly when you share nothing concrete with the people you are in a coalition with.

PROMO 3
VO: The DA’s Mayor in Nelson Mandela Bay got the boot this week –as the EFF jumped sides.

DLAMINI: // Once you start thinking that land must not go back to its original owner, // then our relationship with you is finished.

VO: Is this the beginning of the end for coalition politics
